ggsaveR: a drop-in ggsave() with extra features

Source: R/ggsaveR-package.R
ggsaveR-package.Rd

ggsaveR masks ggplot2::ggsave() with a version whose extra behaviour is controlled entirely by global options. Load the package and set the options at the top of a script, and every existing ggsave() call picks them up.

Options

Set the options with ggsaveR_options(), which checks them, or with options() using the names below.

ggsaveR.formats

NULL (default), a character vector of devices, or a list of lists that each hold a device, optional ggsave() arguments such as width, height, units and dpi, and an optional suffix. One file is written per format.

ggsaveR.size_suffix

"auto" (default), TRUE or FALSE. Add the size to file names, as in plot_120x80mm_300dpi.png; "auto" does so only when file names would otherwise clash.

ggsaveR.dir

NULL (default) or a directory for all plots with a relative file name. Created if needed.

ggsaveR.overwrite_action

"overwrite" (default), "unique" or "stop".

ggsaveR.variants

NULL (default) or any of "greyscale", "deutan", "protan" and "tritan". Also save these versions as PNG files; see preview_variants().

ggsaveR.embed_data

FALSE (default) or TRUE. Embed reproducibility data in PNG files; see read_ggsaveR_data().

ggsaveR.embed_metadata

Which parts to embed: any of "plot", "data", "session_info" and "call" (default: all).

ggsaveR.embed_max_size

Largest size in bytes of the embedded plot object and data (default 5 MB).

ggsaveR.creator

NULL (default) or a string stored as the Author text field of PNG files.

ggsaveR.log

NULL (default) or the path of a CSV file that records every saved file.

Metadata (ggsaveR.embed_data and ggsaveR.creator) is only written to PNG files; other formats are saved unchanged.

Masking

ggsaveR attaches ggplot2 when it is loaded, so ggsaveR::ggsave() masks ggplot2::ggsave() regardless of the order of the library() calls. Use ggplot2::ggsave() or ggsave(..., guard = TRUE) to reach the original.
